correctness.rationale: PASS: For k=2m the target set is exactly 2^m complement-reversal-fixed edges of the binary order-(k−1) de Bruijn graph. Every cyclic host can be rotated to start at P_m=0^m1^m. BFS states (suffix-of-length k−1, bitmask of witnessed target edges) with its forced first edge have a bijection with such rooted indexed cycles; BFS distance and layerwise shortest-path counts give C_m,R_m. The distinct Held–Karp shortest overlap-route recurrence gives matching minimum cyclic cover lengths: distinct required occurrences along any cycle have gaps ≥k−longest proper suffix-prefix overlap, while an overlap tour spells a cycle with those factors. I independently compiled a different C++ BFS and checked exhaustive values m=1: (2,1), m=2:(9,2), m=3:(26,14), m=4:(67,1232); m=4 first optimum discovered after 4,190,096 BFS states. A separate Python subset-DP returned minima 2,9,26,67 and directly tested the 67-symbol witness contains all 16 targets. Enumerative result is finite m≤4, not an infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: PASS best of knowledge: earlier RC-complete sequence constructions require covering one representative for EACH reverse-complement pair of ALL k-mers; the RC-fixed-point antipalindromes are compulsory but are only a tiny target subset, so the optimum and the number of rooted optimal cycles are not determined by those designs. Constrained-language de Bruijn Euler circuits aim at once-each admissible-edge coverage; general cyclic cover and reversal-superstring problems use different target sets/allowed orientations. No exact finite table (2,9,26,67) or rooted multiplicities located in inspected sources; a directly related publisher study could not be examined completely and remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: The 2013 RC-complete paper was read in lawfully accessible full HTML, but a closely related 2016 publisher item was not inspected in full; overlapping fixed-palindrome examples are possible.
